record.question: Which medication is commonly used in acute agitation due to psychosis when non-pharmacologic measures fail?
record.explanation: Answer A: Haloperidol. When nonpharmacologic de-escalation is insufficient, an antipsychotic such as haloperidol may be used for acute psychotic agitation under clinical protocols. Source/context note: Choice, route, dose, and monitoring depend on cause, risks, and local emergency protocol; diazepam is not appropriate for all patients. Reference: https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng10. Verified worked solution, unofficial. Original printed wording and option order reviewed; no matching examiner key is asserted.
